question: same weights, same card: do this branch, colibri origin/dev and llama.cpp b12676 answer a real task equally well, and how fast?

benchmark.gsm8k: the first 60 items of OpenAI's grade-school-math test.jsonl (real ground truth: the number after ####)
benchmark.code: 60 Python-tracing items from 20 one-line templates (seed 20261126); gold = what `python3 -c <snippet>` actually prints, run by the harness, not written by hand
benchmark.protocol: one prompt a line through each engine, the model's own chat framing as literal text (<|message_system|> Thinking effort level: 0, <|message_user|>, <|message_model|><|content_text|>), greedy, n_predict 192, exact match on the value after the prompt's '####' anchor
benchmark.why_not_swebench: SWE-bench needs an agent loop, a container and a much larger model; on 11.7 GB of IQ3_XXS every engine would score 0 and the table would say nothing about the engines

engines.tier: n/a (12 layers' experts on the CPU)

result.quality: a four-way tie: 60 GSM8K items put a 1-sigma of +-5.6 points on each cell, so a 1-2 item spread (73-77%) is noise; the execution-grounded code task is at the ceiling for every engine (59/60, the one miss is the same item)
result.speed_on_this_workload: this branch 33.5-35.0 tok/s aggregate decode, origin/dev 33.8, llama.cpp 22.2 (-34%); the branch and dev tie at short context (same code, the long-context kernels are not exercised here)
result.which_is_best: no engine is better on quality here; the branch and dev tie on speed at this workload, and llama.cpp is a third behind. The branch's real advantage is the long-context cells this benchmark does not reach (typed KV: 64K and 250K on this card, PLAN 15.18/15.19)

the_nondeterminism_finding.measured: two runs of the SAME configuration (this branch, INK2_SPEC=0) produced the same text on 47/120 items; the same-config budgets were 2512 and 2492 experts, the pin sets 1104 and 1176. INK2_SPEC=1 vs a same-budget INK2_SPEC=0 (2492 both) agreed on 50/120 texts.
the_nondeterminism_finding.conclusion: the engine's greedy text is not reproducible across processes on this box (the PLAN already says so for the oracle: it needs OMP_NUM_THREADS=1 and COLI_CUDA=0). Free-form prompts sit close enough to ties that a bit-level difference anywhere flips the text within ~100 tokens; the 120-item text comparison therefore MEASURES THE ENGINE'S OWN RUN-TO-RUN VARIATION, not the speculative path.
the_nondeterminism_finding.what_still_stands: on the three long cells (PLAN 15.19) the spec-on and spec-off runs were token-identical back to back, and a one-item probe (plain step vs a one-draft verify) produced the same 24 tokens; answers across engines agree on 109/120 items (dev vs llama.cpp), i.e. the same model with different numerics
the_nondeterminism_finding.not_isolated: where the run-to-run difference comes from (host MoE accumulation order, the tier's per-run pinning, or OpenMP scheduling) is not isolated; it is not the speculative path, since spec-off vs spec-off shows the same rate
